Component-wise Reference for Maintainability Variance

Source: R/04_main.R
vcov_main_sl.Rd

Compute the pointwise asymptotic variance of maintainability using the component-wise covariance expansion of Sadek and Limnios (2002). The full Markov chain must be irreducible.

Usage

vcov_main_sl(x, time, down)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

time

A single nonnegative integer giving the discrete time point. Values must be less than .Machine$integer.max; missing and infinite values are not allowed.

down

Integer-valued numeric vector of state positions or character vector of state names giving the non-operational states. Missing values are not allowed. Duplicates are ignored; empty and full state sets are valid. States are used in their order in x.

Value

A numeric scalar containing the variance in the \(\sqrt{n}\) limit of the maintainability estimator. Divide by the number of observed transitions \(n\) to approximate the variance of the estimator itself. This is a pointwise variance, not a joint covariance across times.

Details

This function calls vcov_dssc_sl() because subtracting down-state survival from one leaves its variance unchanged. The underlying reference applies Theorem 6 (p. 1850) of Sadek and Limnios (2002) to the down-state block, including every unordered pairwise covariance as documented in vcov_rel_sl(). The initial distribution is fixed and is not renormalized on down. Time zero has variance zero. The reference constructs a dense component covariance and is intended for small down-state blocks.

References

Sadek, A., and Limnios, N. (2002). Asymptotic properties for maximum likelihood estimators for reliability and failure rates of Markov chains. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 31(10), 1837–1861. doi:10.1081/STA-120014916 .

See also

main(), vcov_main(), vcov_dssc_sl()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(0, 1), P)
main(x, time = 0:3, down = 2L)
#> [1] 0.000 0.300 0.510 0.657
vcov_main(x, time = 3L, down = 2L)
#> [1] 1.134472
vcov_main_sl(x, time = 3L, down = 2L)
#> [1] 1.134472
